notes: a security pass. The JavaScript sandboxes lose IndexedDB, the cache storage and BroadcastChannel: an expression the model writes — calculate, json_query, a plugin manifest's transform — runs in a Worker on this origin, and could until now read every chat, memory and folder handle stored here and hand it back. Importing a backup applies looks and behaviour on the first question and asks again, item by item, about the settings that decide where your data goes — the LiteLLM address your key is sent to, the Pyodide script, proxies, the system prompt, the chat mode — and about every 'always allow' rule it carries; both default to no. HTML previews can no longer open windows or show browser dialogs, closing the one way out of a frame that a Content-Security-Policy does not cover. The connector extension binds a file:// grant to a single folder instead of every file on the disk. web_search asks once per provider, the way web_fetch asks once per site. memory_save counts as a write, so it asks and Plan mode refuses it. A permission prompt can show the whole of a long argument instead of its first 4000 characters. And the pdf.js worker, the one CDN file here that carried no checksum, is verified before it runs
